headings.title: Department creation and coordination role
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Department of Public Safety under a director appointed by the governor to coordinate public safety programs.

headings.title: Highway Patrol type II transfer and governance
headings.reviewNote: Transfers State Highway Patrol to department, preserving superintendent appointments, merit selection, and retirement funds.

headings.title: Liquor Control type II transfer and appointments
headings.reviewNote: Transfers Supervisor of Liquor Control to department, providing for governor appointment, deputy hiring, and removal rules.

headings.title: Safety and Fire Prevention Bureau transfer
headings.reviewNote: Transfers safety and fire prevention bureau by type I transfer to the director of public safety.

headings.title: State Fire Marshal type I transfer
headings.reviewNote: Transfers state fire marshal powers, duties, and functions to the department by type I transfer.

headings.title: Law Enforcement Assistance Council transfer
headings.reviewNote: Transfers federal grant functions of law enforcement assistance council to director and abolishes council.

headings.title: Motor vehicle regulations and safety compact
headings.reviewNote: Transfers vehicle regulations and safety compact membership under chapter 307 to director of public safety.

headings.title: Water Patrol creation and subsequent highway transfer
headings.reviewNote: Transfers boat commission to Water Patrol, and transfers water patrol to highway patrol effective January 1, 2011.

headings.title: Veterans' Commission assignment to department
headings.reviewNote: Assigns the Missouri Veterans' Commission under chapter 42 to the department of public safety.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and chapter 536 compliance
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 compliance and nonseverability provisions rendering post-August 28, 2009 rulemaking invalid if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 subsections for 650.005 establishing the Department of Public Safety, agency transfers, and chapter 536 rulemaking compliance (effective 12-08-22 per § 41.036; footnote notes 'Missouri state water patrol' changed to 'water patrol division' by § 306.010, 2010).

headings.title: Operation Payback establishment and reward reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Establishes Operation Payback within the department and, subject to appropriation, authorizes up to $250 reimbursement per reward for tips leading to a methamphetamine seizure.

headings.title: Definition of crime tip organization
headings.reviewNote: Defines crime tip organization as a community, law enforcement, and media partnership encouraging anonymous tips through cash rewards leading to criminal arrests.

headings.title: Eligibility requirements for organization reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director expenditures to reimburse crime tip organizations meeting three requirements: active board with local law enforcement, prior registration, and payment/seizure proof.

headings.title: Five thousand dollar annual reimbursement cap
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any crime tip organization from receiving more than five thousand dollars during any fiscal year.

headings.title: Mandatory administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of public safety to promulgate necessary administrative rules pursuant to chapter 536 and section 650.005.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 650.020 establishing Operation Payback methamphetamine crime tip reimbursements, eligibility criteria, $5,000 fiscal-year cap, and rulemaking (rewrote all 5 fabricated draft headings; note duplicated phrase in source sub. 3(3)).

headings.title: Missing endangered persons advisory system creation
headings.reviewNote: Creates an advisory system to aid in the identification and location of missing endangered persons.

headings.title: Definition of missing endangered person
headings.reviewNote: Defines missing endangered person across three categories: dependent physical/mental disability, circumstances indicating danger to safety, or involuntary/unknown circumstances.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department rules establishing recommended advisory procedures subject to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2007 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 650.025 creating the missing endangered persons advisory system, statutory definition, and rulemaking authority (rewrote all 3 fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: Missouri Law Enforcement Assistance Program creation
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Law Enforcement Assistance Program within the department of public safety.

headings.title: Program purpose and eligible pilot activities
headings.reviewNote: States program purpose to provide financial and technical assistance for local law enforcement pilot programs including specialized training overtime, analytical capacity, and research-based community policing.

headings.title: Contractual fund distribution and state audits
headings.reviewNote: Directs distribution of state funds or technical assistance by annually negotiable contracts and requires periodic audits by the state auditor.

headings.title: Receipt of federal and local funds
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section prohibits any law enforcement agency from receiving available federal or local funds.

headings.title: Eligible municipal and county law enforcement agencies
headings.reviewNote: Specifies eligibility for municipal and county law enforcement agencies in three population-defined county classifications under department standards.

headings.title: Appropriation prerequisite for state expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits expenditure of state funds unless appropriated by the general assembly for this purpose.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 650.035 creating the Missouri Law Enforcement Assistance Program for local pilot programs, contracts, audits, county eligibility, and appropriations (rewrote fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: Definitions for violent crime clearance grants
headings.reviewNote: Defines clearance rates, offense cleared by an arrest, and offense cleared by exceptional means (including four criteria).

headings.title: Missouri Violent Crime Clearance Grant Program creation
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Violent Crime Clearance Grant Program within the department in consultation with POST, the office for victims of crime, and the crime laboratory review commission.

headings.title: Purpose to increase violent crime clearance rates
headings.reviewNote: States that the program's purpose is to improve law enforcement strategies and initiatives aimed at increasing violent crime clearance rates.

headings.title: Allowable uses of grant funding
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates eleven allowable uses including investigator hiring, forensics, IT systems, wellness, and victim coordination.

headings.title: Funding priority criteria for low clearance
headings.reviewNote: Gives priority to agencies with low clearance rates, community partnerships, and investigative evaluation metrics.

headings.title: Mandatory annual reporting by recipient agencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reports on personnel hired, forensic processing, training, tech acquired, and impact on clearance rates.

headings.title: Contractual distribution and state audits
headings.reviewNote: Directs fund distribution by annual contracts and authorizes periodic audits by the state auditor.

headings.title: Receipt of federal and local funds
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that grant recipients are not prohibited from receiving federal or local funds.

headings.title: Appropriation requirement for grant expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no state funds shall be expended under this section unless appropriated by the general assembly.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 650.040 establishing the Missouri Violent Crime Clearance Grant Program, definitions, 11 eligible uses, priorities, annual reporting, contracts, and audits (rewrote shifted/fabricated subs. 1–3; source footnotes note 'Subsection 2' and 'Subsection 3' appear in original rolls for subs. 4 and 5 references).

headings.title: DNA Profiling System creation and purpose
headings.reviewNote: Directs department to develop and establish DNA profiling system to assist in investigations and missing person identification.

headings.title: Approved forensic laboratory composition
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that DNA profiling system consists of qualified Missouri forensic laboratories approved by FBI.

headings.title: Highway Patrol crime lab administrator role
headings.reviewNote: Designates Missouri State Highway Patrol crime laboratory as administrator of state's DNA index system.

headings.title: Compatibility with Federal Bureau of Investigation
headings.reviewNote: Requires system compatibility with FBI to ensure data exchangeability and adherence to national quality standards.

headings.title: Analysis limitations and statutory consistency
headings.reviewNote: Restricts analysis of DNA samples to purposes authorized by statute and applicable federal regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 650.050 establishing the statewide DNA Profiling System, FBI-approved laboratories, highway patrol administration, FBI compatibility, and analysis limits.

headings.title: Functions and purposes of DNA profiling
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates system purposes including criminal investigations, forensic validation studies, and human remains identification.

headings.title: Central repository and CODIS collaboration
headings.reviewNote: Designates highway patrol as central repository and requires collaboration with FBI in CODIS and NDIS.

headings.title: Rulemaking for biological sample collection
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes highway patrol rules in accordance with FBI standards for sample collection under section 536.024.

headings.title: Sample collection by custodial agencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires highway patrol to provide collection components and assigns sample/fingerprint collection to corrections, city or county jails, sentencing court sheriffs for contracted supervision, and sex offender registering agencies.

headings.title: Forwarding of specimens and appropriation condition
headings.reviewNote: Requires specimens to be forwarded to patrol lab and subjects state or county DNA profiling to appropriations.

headings.title: Quality assurance standards for laboratories
headings.reviewNote: Mandates participating forensic laboratories to meet FBI and highway patrol quality assurance standards.

headings.title: Court testimony and presentation assistance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes participating laboratories to assist prosecutors and provide expert testimony on DNA evidence in court.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants department rulemaking authority subject to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2004 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 650.052 governing DNA profiling system duties, CODIS repository, sample collection agencies, quality standards, court testimony, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Individuals subject to fingerprint and DNA collection
headings.reviewNote: Requires fingerprint and biological sample collection from persons found guilty of felonies or chapter 566 offenses, arrestees 17+ for burglary or specified felonies, sexually violent predators, and sex offender registrants.

headings.title: Required timing and settings for DNA sample submission
headings.reviewNote: Specifies six points at which subject individuals must provide DNA samples, including booking, corrections reception/release, jails or SVP facilities, interstate compacts, probation/parole, and sex offender registration.

headings.title: Enforcement, immunity, use of force, and refusal
headings.reviewNote: Tasks highway patrol and corrections with enforcement without right of refusal, grants reasonable-collection immunity, permits necessary force, directs revocation recommendations for refusal, and requires resampling if inadequate.

headings.title: Consistency with state and FBI DNA databank rules
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits procedures and rules for collection, analysis, storage, expungement, use, and privacy from conflicting with Missouri DNA profiling system and FBI databank rules.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for unauthorized DNA disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unauthorized use or dissemination of individually identifiable DNA database information for non-criminal-justice purposes as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Implementation subject to future appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Subjects implementation of sections 650.050 to 650.100 to future appropriations to maintain compatibility with the FBI DNA databank.

headings.title: Closed record status and authorized DNA disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Designates DNA records and biological materials as closed records under chapter 610, strictly confidential except for five enumerated categories including law enforcement, prosecutors, the subject/counsel, and judges.

headings.title: Restricted use and confidentiality of obtained records
headings.reviewNote: Limits recipients' use of DNA records to investigative, prosecutorial, and law enforcement identification purposes (including human remains) and preserves strict confidentiality.

headings.title: Expungement upon reversal, vacated plea, or section 568.040
headings.reviewNote: Establishes court-ordered DNA expungement procedures, 30-day laboratory notice, exception for shared physical evidence, and bar against evidentiary suppression or conviction invalidation for expungement delay.

headings.title: Expungement when prosecutor declines arrestee prosecution
headings.reviewNote: Requires arresting agency notice within 90 days of declined prosecution and highway patrol laboratory expungement and sample destruction within 30 days absent other qualifying offenses or arrests.

headings.title: Expungement upon withdrawn charges, dismissal, or acquittal
headings.reviewNote: Requires prosecutor or court notice upon withdrawn charges, dismissal, no probable cause, or not guilty verdict, and 30-day laboratory determination and expungement absent other qualifying offenses or arrests.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 11 subsections for 650.055 governing mandatory DNA collection categories and timing, enforcement/immunity, FBI rule consistency, confidentiality, and expungement procedures (rewrote all 11 shifted/fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: Restrictions on local law enforcement DNA systems
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits local law enforcement agencies from establishing or operating a DNA system unless compatible with state/FBI systems, capable of data exchange, and nonconflicting in rules.

headings.title: Mandatory departmental rulemaking for local systems
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Missouri department of public safety to adopt rules implementing this section.

headings.title: Individual case DNA analysis and appropriations condition
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that local agencies may perform DNA profiling in individual criminal cases for court presentation and subjects sections 650.050 to 650.057 (except 650.050) to future appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 650.057 restricting local law enforcement DNA systems, mandating DPS rules, and permitting individual-case DNA analysis (rewrote all 3 fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: Restitution for actually innocent individuals and limits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes $179/day postconviction restitution (capped at $65,000/year, pro rata if underfunded, no interest) and nonmonetary relief for actually innocent felons, defines actual innocence, and bars other civil redress.

headings.title: Liability and sanctions when DNA confirms guilt
headings.reviewNote: Makes petitioners under section 547.035 whose DNA test confirms guilt liable for reasonable testing costs and subject to sanctions under section 217.262.

headings.title: Personal nonassignable nature of restitution petitions
headings.reviewNote: Restricts filing to the actually innocent individual or legal guardian, prohibits assignment or filing by heirs, and terminates state payment obligations upon death.

headings.title: Automatic expungement order and restoration of status
headings.reviewNote: Grants automatic expungement of arrest, plea, trial, and conviction records to actually innocent individuals, makes proceedings confidential, restores prior status, and bars perjury liability for nondisclosure.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 650.058 governing restitution for actually innocent individuals, sanctions when DNA confirms guilt, nonassignability, and automatic expungement (rewrote all 4 fabricated draft headings; source note cites severability clause § 1.1001).

headings.title: Crime Laboratory Review Commission establishment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Crime Laboratory Review Commission within the department of public safety to independently review state-funded Missouri crime laboratories.

headings.title: Commission membership composition and qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Specifies five citizen members: an accredited crime lab senior manager, a county/municipal law enforcement manager, a prosecutor, a criminal defense attorney, and the DPS director or designee.

headings.title: Governor appointment and term lengths
headings.reviewNote: Governs gubernatorial appointments with senate consent, staggered initial two- and four-year terms, subsequent four-year terms, and vacancy appointments.

headings.title: Vacancy upon loss of appointment qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Deems a commission member's seat vacant if the member no longer meets the qualifications for which appointed.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and direct expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that commission members receive no compensation other than reimbursement for costs directly associated with executing commission duties.

headings.title: Chair designation, annual meetings, and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Designates the DPS director or designee as chairman, requires at least annual meetings, and sets a three-member quorum.

headings.title: Definition of crime laboratory
headings.reviewNote: Defines crime laboratory as public facility employing scientists who examine evidence and testify in state courts.

headings.title: Investigatory and oversight powers of commission
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates six commission powers including laboratory capability assessments, misconduct investigations, and reprimands.

headings.title: Annual activity report to governor
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual report to governor summarizing activities and suggestions, barring relocation recommendations.

headings.title: Department authority to revoke grant money
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department to revoke grant funds from laboratories that fail to cooperate or engage in serious misconduct.

headings.title: Mandatory member recusal for employer conflicts
headings.reviewNote: Requires lab managers and officers on commission to recuse themselves from votes concerning their employing laboratories.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 11 subsections for 650.059 establishing the five-member Crime Laboratory Review Commission, terms, vacancies, meetings, oversight powers, annual report, grant revocation, and recusals (fixed wrong member counts/terms in subs. 1–3 and rewrote shifted/fabricated subs. 4–6).

headings.title: Mandatory crime laboratory accreditation requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires crime laboratories providing reports or testimony to a state court on or after December 31, 2012, to be accredited or provisionally accredited by a department-approved body.

headings.title: Grandfather clause for pre-2012 forensic analyses
headings.reviewNote: Exempts forensic analyses, reports, and evidence produced prior to December 31, 2012, from accreditation requirement.

headings.title: Use of section 595.045 funds for accreditation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes crime laboratories to use funding provided through section 595.045 to defray costs of applying for and maintaining accreditation.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and nonseverability with chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules identifying approved accrediting bodies and compliance monitoring, subject to chapter 536 and post-August 28, 2008 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 650.060 establishing crime laboratory accreditation on or after December 31, 2012, pre-cutoff exemption, section 595.045 funding, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Crime Laboratory Assistance Program creation
headings.reviewNote: Creates Missouri Crime Laboratory Assistance Program within department to defray laboratory operational costs.

headings.title: Appropriation of court cost collections
headings.reviewNote: Provides that funds collected pursuant to section 488.029 shall be appropriated to department for program.

headings.title: Contractual distribution of funds and state audits
headings.reviewNote: Directs fund distribution by annual contracts and requires periodic audits of recipient labs by state auditor.

headings.title: Receipt of federal and local funds
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that program statutes do not prohibit crime laboratories from receiving federal or local funds.

headings.title: Law enforcement agency access to laboratories
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees municipal, county, and state law enforcement agencies access to state-funded crime laboratories.

headings.title: Appropriations condition for fund expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits expenditure of state funds under program unless specifically appropriated by the general assembly.

headings.title: Legislative authorization for new laboratories
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits starting new crime laboratories with state funds until authorized by the general assembly.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 650.105 establishing the Missouri Crime Laboratory Assistance Program, funding contracts, audits, agency access, appropriations, and new-laboratory limits.

headings.title: Cyber Crime Investigation Fund creation
headings.reviewNote: Creates Cyber Crime Investigation Fund in state treasury administered by department for cyber crime grants.

headings.title: Grant program for multijurisdictional task forces
headings.reviewNote: Directs department to distribute grants to task forces investigating internet sex crimes against children.

headings.title: Grant panel composition and member appointments
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a nine-member grant panel (DPS director/designee, six law enforcement association nominees serving four-year terms, and one house and one senate member) with mileage reimbursement only.

headings.title: Local matching fund and in-kind requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires local matching amounts (new/existing funds or in-kind equipment/personnel) as determined by appropriations or the panel to receive grants.

headings.title: Priority for newly hired detectives and forensic staff
headings.reviewNote: States that priority in awarding grants should be given to newly hired detectives and computer forensic personnel.

headings.title: Minimum training standards for grant personnel
headings.reviewNote: Directs the panel to establish minimum training standards for detectives and computer forensic personnel participating in the grant program.

headings.title: Information sharing and highway patrol cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating task forces and agencies to share information and cooperate with the highway patrol and existing internet crimes against children task force programs.

headings.title: Panel recommendations to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the panel to make recommendations to the general assembly regarding the need for additional resources or appropriations.

headings.title: Statewide power of arrest for task force officers
headings.reviewNote: Grants active task force officers statewide arrest power within investigation scope with prior notice to local chief or sheriff (or as soon as practical in exigent circumstances).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 650.120 creating the Cyber Crime Investigation Fund, grant program and panel, local matching, training standards, cooperation, and statewide arrest powers (rewrote fabricated draft subs. 4–9).

headings.title: Multijurisdictional enforcement groups establishment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes two or more political subdivisions, or the highway patrol with political subdivisions, to form a multijurisdictional enforcement group for computer, internet-based, narcotics, and drug investigations.

headings.title: Statewide power of arrest and local notification
headings.reviewNote: Grants active MEG peace officers statewide arrest power within investigation scope with prior notice to local chief or sheriff (or as soon as practical in exigent circumstances) and optional local cooperation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.156 authorizing multijurisdictional enforcement groups and statewide arrest powers with local notice (rewrote fabricated draft sub. 2; transferred 2014, formerly § 195.505, effective 1-02-17).

headings.title: Interstate agreements by bordering counties for MEGs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a border county to enter into an agreement under section 70.220 with political subdivisions in a contiguous out-of-state county to form a drug-enforcement MEG.

headings.title: Deputization and certification of out-of-state officers
headings.reviewNote: Permits deputization of contiguous-state officers who meet their home state's peace officer training and certification standards for investigations and arrests under section 650.156.

headings.title: Powers and immunities of out-of-state officers
headings.reviewNote: Extends the same powers and immunities under section 70.815 to out-of-state officers working under an interstate MEG agreement as to Missouri political subdivision officers.

headings.title: Eligibility of interstate MEGs for state grants
headings.reviewNote: Makes a multijurisdictional enforcement group formed under this section eligible to receive state operating grants under section 650.161.

headings.title: Reciprocity condition for interstate MEG provisions
headings.reviewNote: Conditions subsections 2, 3, and 4 on the other state providing legal authority for its political subdivisions to enter reciprocal agreements and extend reciprocal powers to Missouri officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 650.159 governing interstate MEG agreements, officer deputization, powers and immunities, grant eligibility, and reciprocity (rewrote all 5 fabricated draft headings; formerly § 195.507, effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: MEG eligibility for state operating grants
headings.reviewNote: Makes any multijurisdictional enforcement group meeting minimum statutory criteria eligible for state grants to help defray operating costs.

headings.title: Six minimum eligibility criteria for MEG grants
headings.reviewNote: Requires intergovernmental contracts, a MEG policy board including local officials and hazmat/fire representatives, a designated financial officer, drug-law focus, DPS cooperation, and local hazmat emergency strategy.

headings.title: Department monitoring, grant certification, and other funds
headings.reviewNote: Directs DPS to monitor grant-funded MEGs and certify grant amounts to the auditor, while preserving lawful funding from other sources.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 650.161 establishing MEG state grant eligibility, six operational criteria, and DPS monitoring (rewrote all 3 fabricated/shifted draft headings; formerly § 195.509, effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Board creation, membership, terms, and meetings
headings.reviewNote: Creates the seven-member Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Rules appointed by the governor with senate consent for four-year staggered terms, specifies represented interests, removal, vacancies, chair election, and quarterly meetings.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and travel expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that board members serve without salary and receive actual traveling and hotel expenses incurred in performing their duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.210 creating the seven-member Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Rules, terms, meetings, and travel expense reimbursement (fixed shifted draft sub. 2).

headings.title: Board rulemaking and adoption of national codes
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to formulate boiler and pressure vessel rules incorporating the ASME Code for new construction, existing-installation rules, and National Board or ANSI/API 510 inspection standards.

headings.title: Force of law and twelve-month installation grace period
headings.reviewNote: Gives board rules the force and effect of law while allowing twelve months after promulgation before new-construction rules prevent installation.

headings.title: Effective timeline for subsequent rule amendments
headings.reviewNote: Makes subsequent rule amendments permissive immediately and mandatory twelve months after promulgation.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Conditions the effectiveness of any rule promulgated under this chapter on compliance with section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 650.215 governing boiler board rulemaking, ASME/National Board/ANSI-API 510 standards, 12-month effective timelines, and section 536.024 compliance (rewrote shifted/fabricated subs. 2–3).

headings.title: Maximum allowable pressure for code-stamped equipment
headings.reviewNote: Determines maximum allowable pressure of ASME or API-ASME code-stamped boilers and pressure vessels under the construction code edition or a properly rerated later ASME edition.

headings.title: Pressure calculation for unstamped and special vessels
headings.reviewNote: Computes maximum allowable pressure of unstamped boilers/vessels under National Board or ANSI/API 510 codes, while authorizing discretionary special permits for specially constructed pressure vessels.

headings.title: Use, sale, and reinstallation of conforming equipment
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 650.200 to 650.290 do not prevent use, sale, or reinstallation of equipment conforming to existing-installation rules and not found unsafe.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 650.225 governing maximum allowable pressure for code-stamped and unstamped boilers/pressure vessels, special permits, and conforming reuse (rewrote all 3 inaccurate/fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: Exempt boilers and pressure vessels enumeration
headings.reviewNote: Exempts nine categories of boilers and pressure vessels from sections 650.200 to 650.290, including federal/state-regulated, LP/compressed gas, vehicle, railroad, small-capacity, farm, hobby, and specified water-treatment vessels.

headings.title: Exemptions from inspection and fee sections
headings.reviewNote: Exempts seven categories from sections 650.260 to 650.275, including cannery vessels, residential/small-apartment heating and hot water boilers, hobby miniature steam models, domestic water heaters, and domestic water pressure vessels.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.230 listing exemptions from the entire boiler act (sub. 1) and from inspection/certificate/fee provisions (sub. 2).

headings.title: Chief inspector appointment and qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to appoint a chief inspector with at least ten years' high-pressure boiler/vessel experience who passed the section 650.250 exam, removable for cause after board investigation and recommendation.

headings.title: Powers and duties of chief inspector
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the chief inspector, if authorized by the director, to enforce boiler laws/rules, maintain inspection records, publish rules, issue/suspend/revoke certificates, prosecute violators, and draw authorized office/travel funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.235 governing chief boiler inspector appointment, qualifications, removal, and six statutory powers and duties (rewrote fabricated draft sub. 2 and corrected sub. 1).

headings.title: Special inspector commissions for insurers and owners
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director, upon request of licensed boiler insurers or companies with approved owner/user pressure-vessel inspection services, to commission qualified inspectors who pass the exam or hold equivalent/National Board credentials.

headings.title: Compensation and commission conditions of special inspectors
headings.reviewNote: Provides that special inspectors receive no state salary and condition commissions on continued company employment.

headings.title: Exemption from state inspection fees upon inspection
headings.reviewNote: Exempts boiler owners from paying state inspection fees when boilers are inspected by commissioned special inspectors.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 650.245 requiring special inspector commissions for insurers and qualifying owner/user inspection services, employment conditions, and state inspection fee exemptions.

headings.title: Written examination for boiler inspector commissions
headings.reviewNote: Requires written examination administered by board for inspector applicants and establishes examination fees.

headings.title: Commission duration and annual renewal fees
headings.reviewNote: Limits inspector commissions to one year, subject to annual renewal upon payment of scheduled renewal fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.250 governing written boiler inspector examinations, 90-day reexamination appeals, fee schedules, and one-year renewable commissions.

headings.title: Suspension of inspector commission and appeal rights
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to suspend an inspector's commission after board investigation/recommendation for incompetence, untrustworthiness, or willful falsification, with written notice within ten days and appeal rights under section 650.285.

headings.title: Board revocation hearing and director action
headings.reviewNote: Requires board hearing on ten days notice and director revocation if inspector is found unqualified.

headings.title: Reinstatement application after ninety days
headings.reviewNote: Allows suspended inspectors to apply for reinstatement ninety days after date of suspension.

headings.title: Replacement of lost or destroyed commissions
headings.reviewNote: Directs issuance of replacement commission without reexamination if original commission is lost or destroyed.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 650.255 governing boiler inspector commission suspension, board revocation hearings, 90-day reinstatement applications, and lost-commission replacement.

headings.title: Free access for boiler premises inspections
headings.reviewNote: Grants director and inspectors free access during reasonable hours to premises where boilers are installed.

headings.title: Mandatory inspection intervals and certificate cycles
headings.reviewNote: Establishes annual inspection cycles for power boilers and biennial cycles for heating and pressure vessels.

headings.title: Inspectors authorized to conduct required inspections
headings.reviewNote: Requires section inspections to be performed by the chief inspector, a deputy inspector, or a special inspector.

headings.title: Owner tests under inspector supervision and fee
headings.reviewNote: Requires owners or users to perform tests deemed necessary for stated cause under inspector supervision and pay the scheduled supervision fee under section 650.275.

headings.title: Construction inspection of boilers and pressure vessels
headings.reviewNote: Requires boilers (except cast iron sectional) and pressure vessels installed after the 12-month rule effective period to be inspected during construction by a state-authorized or National Board-commissioned inspector.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 650.260 governing inspector premises access, inspection intervals, authorized inspectors, supervised cause tests, and construction inspections (rewrote inaccurate/fabricated draft subs. 4–5).

headings.title: Special inspector reports and certificate issuance
headings.reviewNote: Requires companies employing special inspectors (except owner/user services) to file certificate inspection reports within 30 days on National Board forms, and provides for fee payment and inspection certificate issuance.

headings.title: Owner-user inspection records and annual certified statements
headings.reviewNote: Requires companies with owner/user pressure-vessel inspection services to maintain accessible inspection records and file an annual engineer-signed compliance statement with filing fee.

headings.title: Termination of certificate when insurance ceases
headings.reviewNote: Invalidates any inspection certificate issued for an insured boiler or pressure vessel upon report of a special inspector once authorized insurance ceases.

headings.title: Suspension of certificate for unsafe conditions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director or authorized representative to suspend an inspection certificate when operation menaces public safety or violates board rules until corrected and reinstated.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 650.265 governing special inspector reports, owner/user inspection records and annual statements, cessation of insurance, and certificate suspension (rewrote fabricated draft subs. 2–3 and corrected subs. 1 and 4).

headings.title: Board authority to establish inspection fees
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board, in consultation with the director, to set fees by rule under section 536.021 reflecting the average of at least 75 percent of regulating states, with biennial survey limits.

headings.title: Payment of state inspection fees upon invoice
headings.reviewNote: Requires boiler owners inspected by state inspectors to pay invoiced fees in accordance with adopted schedule.

headings.title: Transfer of collected fees to department director
headings.reviewNote: Directs chief inspector to transfer all collected inspection fees to the director of public safety.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 650.275 governing boiler inspection fee rules benchmarked to regulating states, owner invoice payment, and fee transfers to the director.

headings.title: Boiler and Pressure Vessels Safety Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates dedicated safety fund, biennially revisable fees, and preserves municipal inspection fee collection.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section or sections 650.210 to 650.275 to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2002 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.277 creating the Boiler and Pressure Vessels Safety Fund, biennial fee authority, municipal fee preservation, and chapter 536 nonseverability.

headings.title: Office for Victims of Crime establishment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Office for Victims of Crime in the department to coordinate crime victim programs/rights, requiring coordinated response in catastrophic crimes and authorizing response upon specific request.

headings.title: Coordination with statewide victim assistance coalitions
headings.reviewNote: Directs office to coordinate with statewide coalitions on domestic violence, sexual assault, and crime reduction.

headings.title: Statewide automated crime victim notification system
headings.reviewNote: Tasks office with assessing, developing, and serving as sole state coordinating agency for automated notification.

headings.title: Procedural administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to promulgate administrative rules and deems rules wholly procedural and without fiscal impact compliant with section 536.016.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 650.310 establishing the Office for Victims of Crime, coalition coordination, statewide automated notification system, and procedural rulemaking (source footnote notes word 'of' appears in original rolls for 'Office for Victims of Crime').

headings.title: Missouri 911 Service Board composition
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates fifteen members including public safety, municipal, EMS, fire, police, sheriff, and telecom representatives.

headings.title: Governor appointment, terms, and corporate restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Governs appointments by governor with senate consent, four-year terms, and limits corporate affiliate representation.

headings.title: Quarterly board meetings and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly meetings, recordkeeping, uncompensated service, and reimbursement for actual expenses.

headings.title: Powers and statutory duties of 911 board
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates twenty-four board duties including 911 technical standards, mediation, state coordinator designation, next-generation 911 planning, grants/loans with 50% match, prepaid wireless rates, regional coordination centers, and public education.

headings.title: Department staff assistance and consultant hiring authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of public safety to provide necessary staff assistance to the board and authorizes the board to hire consultants.

headings.title: Board rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to promulgate rules implementing sections 190.455 to 190.475 and 650.320 to 650.340, subject to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2017 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 650.330 establishing Missouri 911 Service Board composition, four-year terms, quarterly meetings, 24 statutory duties, staff/consultants, and rulemaking (rewrote fabricated draft subs. 5–6 and fixed duty count in sub. 4).

headings.title: Eligible applicants, technical reports, and cooperative projects
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes qualifying counties, home rule cities, regional planning commissions, and elected emergency services boards to apply for 911 project loans with a technical assistance report and allows cooperative projects.

headings.title: Cost recovery assurance and governing body approval
headings.reviewNote: Restricts loan approval to applicants demonstrating project cost recovery during the repayment period and submitting written governing-body approval of the loan agreement.

headings.title: Board schedule for approving or disapproving applications
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to approve or disapprove loan applications delivered by certified/registered mail or hand delivery on a board-determined schedule.

headings.title: Loan repayment terms and interest rates
headings.reviewNote: Requires loan recipients to repay loans with interest at the board-required rate on payment schedules determined by the board.

headings.title: Annual budgeting for required loan payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires each loan recipient to annually budget an amount at least sufficient to make required payments.

headings.title: Credit of loan repayments to 911 trust fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs principal and interest repayments to be credited to the Missouri 911 service trust fund under section 190.420.

headings.title: Revenue deduction upon sixty-day payment default
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to notify the revenue director upon a 60-day payment default to deduct overdue amounts first from prepaid wireless charges and next from local sales tax distributions.

headings.title: Remittance of payments and immediate fund deposit
headings.reviewNote: Requires loan recipients to remit subsection 4 payments to the board or its designee for immediate deposit into the Missouri 911 service trust fund.

headings.title: Restricted loan uses and default recovery actions
headings.reviewNote: Restricts loan funds to approved application/agreement purposes and directs the board to recover full loan amounts and remedies upon misuse or unresolved default.

headings.title: Initiation of statutory deduction collection after default
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the board to initiate subsection 7 collection actions if a borrower fails to remit repayment within sixty days of the due date.

headings.title: Collection actions with attorney general for other entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the board, with advice and consent of the attorney general, to initiate collection actions against borrowers not covered by statutory deduction procedures.

headings.title: Discretionary board audits of loans and grants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the board, at its discretion, to audit expenditures of any loan, grant, or expenditure or computation of payments.

headings.title: Application bar for unreturned annual PSAP survey
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the board from approving any application if the applicant failed to return the annual public safety answering point survey required under section 650.330.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 13 subsections for 650.335 governing 911 communications project loans, eligibility, repayment, 60-day default interceptions, audits, and survey prerequisites (rewrote all 13 fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: Short title as 911 Training and Standards Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates the section as the 911 Training and Standards Act.

headings.title: Initial training hours for telecommunicator first responders
headings.reviewNote: Sets initial training requirements of 16 hours each for police, fire, and EMS telecommunicator first responders and 40 hours for joint communication center telecommunicators.

headings.title: Ongoing continuing training requirement every three years
headings.reviewNote: Requires employed telecommunicator first responders to complete at least twenty-four hours of ongoing training every three years from board-authorized providers.

headings.title: Grandfather exemption and twelve-month completion deadline
headings.reviewNote: Exempts telecommunicators employed on August 28, 1999, from initial training and requires those hired after August 28, 1999, to complete initial training within twelve months.

headings.title: Waiver for equivalent out-of-state training
headings.reviewNote: Waives initial training requirements upon proof to the committee of completing out-of-state training at least as stringent as subsection 2.

headings.title: Board rule designating authorized training providers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to determine by administrative rule the persons or organizations authorized to conduct required training.

headings.title: Emergency medical dispatcher course approval and rules
headings.reviewNote: Makes the board responsible for approving emergency medical dispatcher courses and developing rules in collaboration with the state EMS medical director's advisory committee.

headings.title: Ambulance memoranda of understanding and medical director
headings.reviewNote: Requires dispatch agencies to maintain memoranda of understanding with dispatched ambulance services and a medical director if providing prearrival medical instructions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 650.340 establishing the 911 Training and Standards Act, initial and ongoing telecommunicator hours, waivers, EMD courses, and dispatch MOUs (rewrote all 8 fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: MoSMART taskforce creation, composition, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Creates MoSMART composed of five sitting sheriffs appointed by the governor from twenty nominees for two-year terms (max three per party), with chair election and expense reimbursement from the MoSMART fund.

headings.title: Taskforce semiannual meetings and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Requires MoSMART to meet at least twice per calendar year with additional meetings called upon request of two members, and defines a majority of appointed members as a quorum.

headings.title: MoSMART Fund creation and annual grant distribution
headings.reviewNote: Creates the MoSMART Fund in the state treasury and directs the DPS director to distribute 50% to 100% annually as MoSMART-approved grants.

headings.title: Fund deposits, administrative cap, and nonreversion
headings.reviewNote: Credits MoSMART moneys to the fund (excluding deputy sheriff and concealed carry funds), caps DPS administrative reimbursement at 1%–2% (0% from deputy sheriff fund), and exempts balances from biennial lapse.

headings.title: Concealed Carry Permit Fund and statewide server system
headings.reviewNote: Creates the nonreverting Concealed Carry Permit Fund for MoSMART-approved grants supporting county concealed carry compliance and a statewide sheriff concealed carry permit server network.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2003 nonseverability.

headings.title: MoSMART grant applications and funding limit
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes county law enforcement and task force grant applications, capping annual awards at one hundred thousand dollars.

headings.title: Anti-methamphetamine grant funding priorities
headings.reviewNote: Establishes three anti-methamphetamine funding priorities favoring multijurisdictional task forces, unfunded HIDTA (High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area) counties, and other justified county needs.

headings.title: Administration of deputy sheriff salary fund
headings.reviewNote: Tasks MoSMART with administering the deputy sheriff salary supplementation fund under section 57.278.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 650.350 establishing MoSMART, the MoSMART Fund, the Concealed Carry Permit Fund, grant caps, HIDTA priorities, and deputy sheriff salary fund administration (rewrote shifted/fabricated draft subs. 1–5; footnote defines HIDTA).

headings.title: County emergency communications commission establishment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes county governing body to establish emergency communications commission with seven appointed commissioners.

headings.title: Commission composition and nominating associations
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates commissioners including police, fire, sheriff, and at-large members from nominating associations.

headings.title: Terms of office, tenure, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Governs staggered five-year commissioner terms, limits service to two consecutive terms, and fills vacancies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 650.393 authorizing seven-member county emergency communications commissions, nominating associations, and staggered five-year terms.

headings.title: County voter submission for communications tax
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commission to request voter referendum on emergency communications property tax or sales tax.

headings.title: Statutory ballot forms for property or sales tax
headings.reviewNote: Specifies exact statutory ballot language for property tax up to six cents or sales tax up to one-tenth percent.

headings.title: Election conduct, levy commencement, and resubmission
headings.reviewNote: Requires majority voter approval, levy in subsequent tax year, and allows resubmission upon voter rejection.

headings.title: Sales tax effective date and twelve-month resubmission bar
headings.reviewNote: Sets sales tax effective date on second quarter after notice, exempts food, and bars resubmission for twelve months.

headings.title: Applicability of general local sales tax statutes
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 32.085 and 32.087 provisions to emergency communications sales taxes except as modified.

headings.title: County Emergency Communications Sales Tax Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates special trust fund for tax collections, one percent state fee, monthly remittance, and investment rules.

headings.title: Repeal or termination notice and fund retention
headings.reviewNote: Requires remaining funds to be used for designated purposes upon repeal/termination, 90-day county notice to revenue director, optional one-year 2% retention for refunds/bad checks, and final balance remittance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 650.399 authorizing county emergency communications property or sales taxes, ballot language, trust fund, and tax repeal procedures (rewrote fabricated draft sub. 7).

headings.title: Payment of system obligations from fund or bonds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes county payment of emergency communications system obligations from the section 650.402 fund or from bonds issued under this section.

headings.title: Bond issuance authority, valuation cap, and terms
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes county bonds payable from authorized taxes up to 6% of assessed real property valuation, in $100 multiples, with commissioner-set interest and maximum 20-year maturity.

headings.title: Voter submission and election notice requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires voter submission when proposing bonds (citing subdivision (3) of subsection 2 in text) and chapter 115 election notice stating the bond amount.

headings.title: Statutory ballot form for bond proposition
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth the statutory yes/no ballot question form for county emergency communications system bond issuance.

headings.title: Voter approval threshold and execution of bonds
headings.reviewNote: Requires entry of election results and directs bond execution upon four-sevenths voter approval unless general state law requires a different majority.

headings.title: Minimum bond sale price and restricted proceeds use
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling bonds below 95% of par value, directs payment to county treasurer and disbursement on warrants, and limits proceeds to election, construction, repair, and maintenance costs.

headings.title: Tax revenue payment source and treasurer reserve
headings.reviewNote: Restricts bond payment to section 650.399 tax revenues, bond proceeds, and interest, and directs the county treasurer to hold interest and 3% principal reserves.

headings.title: Priority of tax revenues and surplus expenditure
headings.reviewNote: Dedicates section 650.399 tax revenues to bond principal and interest while allowing excess funds (less 3% principal reserve) to be used under section 650.411.

headings.title: Delivery of sold bonds and cancellation upon payment
headings.reviewNote: Directs the county treasurer to deliver sold bonds upon commissioner order, cancel paid bonds, and deliver cancelled bonds to the county clerk.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 650.408 governing county emergency communications system bond issuance, 6% valuation cap, voter ballot form, 4/7 approval, 95% par floor, reserves, and cancellation (rewrote all 9 fabricated draft headings; note sub. 3 internal reference to 'subdivision (3) of subsection 2').

headings.title: Public Safety Officer Medal of Valor establishment
headings.reviewNote: Creates Missouri Public Safety Officer Medal of Valor awarded by governor to public safety officers for exceptional bravery.

headings.title: Posthumous presentation to surviving relatives by priority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes posthumous medal presentation to a surviving relative in statutory order: unremarried widow, eldest living son, eldest living daughter, father, mother, eldest living brother, eldest living sister, and eldest living grandchild.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.454 authorizing gubernatorial awards of the Missouri Public Safety Officer Medal of Valor and posthumous presentation order (rewrote fabricated draft sub. 2).

headings.title: Medal of Valor Review Board establishment and membership
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the eleven-member Missouri Medal of Valor Review Board composed of Missouri residents with public safety expertise, including DPS director/designee, chief, fire chief, sheriff, ambulance director, four citizen experts, and two governor appointees.

headings.title: Four-year term of board members
headings.reviewNote: Sets the term of each board member at four years.

headings.title: Vacancies not affecting board powers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a membership vacancy does not affect board powers and shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment.

headings.title: Board organization, meetings, nominations, confidentiality, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Governs chair election, meetings (1–3 annually), quorum/rules, annual selection of up to seven medal nominees (increasable by governor), agency information requests, investigation confidentiality, and expense reimbursement from the section 650.460 fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 650.457 establishing the eleven-member Missouri Medal of Valor Review Board, four-year terms, vacancies, and operational/nomination procedures (rewrote shifted/inaccurate draft subs. 1–4).

headings.title: Public Safety Officer Medal of Valor Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates dedicated fund in state treasury administered by office of administration with nonreversion.

headings.title: Authorized fund expenditure purposes
headings.reviewNote: Restricts fund moneys solely to reimbursing review board travel expenses and promoting design solicitation, manufacture, and distribution of the Missouri public safety medal of valor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 650.460 creating the nonreverting Missouri Public Safety Officer Medal of Valor Fund and restricting expenditure purposes.

headings.title: Prohibition on restricting federal immigration cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits government entities from restricting communications or cooperation with federal immigration officials.

headings.title: Fingerprint identification data sharing with federal database
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes municipalities and political subdivisions to collect and share biometric data through federal IAFIS.

headings.title: Protection of public employees communicating immigration status
headings.reviewNote: Bars restrictions on public employees maintaining, sending, or exchanging immigration status information with agencies.

headings.title: Attorney general opinion requests on noncompliant policies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any legislator, upon resident complaint or prior to funding/grants, to request an attorney general opinion on whether a government entity has policies contravening subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: State funding bar for noncompliant local entities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits state agencies or departments from providing funding or monetary grants to any government entity determined under subsection 4 to have a policy contravening subsections 1 and 3 until repealed or no longer in effect.

headings.title: Exemption for federal public benefit administration
headings.reviewNote: Exempts agencies administering federal public benefit programs under 8 U.S.C. Section 1612 from prohibitions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 650.475 barring restrictions on federal immigration communication/cooperation, authorizing IAFIS identity sharing, protecting public employees, enabling AG opinions and funding bars, and exempting 8 U.S.C. 1612 agencies.

headings.title: Statewide Blue Alert System establishment
headings.reviewNote: Creates statewide Blue Alert System to aid in apprehending individuals suspected of killing or seriously wounding officers.

headings.title: Definition of law enforcement officer
headings.reviewNote: Defines law enforcement officer as public servants authorized to make arrests, including armed federal officers.

headings.title: Department coordination and regional broadcast alerts
headings.reviewNote: Directs department to establish regions and coordinate local law enforcement agencies and commercial broadcasters.

headings.title: Participating state agencies and lottery dissemination
headings.reviewNote: Includes department of public safety, highway patrol, transportation department, and Missouri lottery in alert system.

headings.title: Department authority to manage alert system
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department of public safety to develop, implement, and manage the statewide blue alert system.

headings.title: Voluntary participation by local agencies and broadcasters
headings.reviewNote: Provides that participation in blue alert system is entirely voluntary for local agencies, broadcasters, and private entities.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for false blue alert reports
headings.reviewNote: Classifies false alert report as class A misdemeanor, elevating to class E felony if injury or death results.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and nonseverability with chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department rulemaking for the blue alert system subject to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2017 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 650.520 creating the statewide Blue Alert System, definitions, regional coordination, participating agencies, voluntary participation, false-report penalties, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Statutory title designation as RJ's Law
headings.reviewNote: Designates section statutory title as RJ's Law.

headings.title: Purple Alert System creation and purpose
headings.reviewNote: Creates statewide Purple Alert System to locate missing persons with developmental disabilities facing credible harm.

headings.title: Definition of qualifying developmental disabilities
headings.reviewNote: Defines developmental disability to include mental/cognitive disabilities (excluding Alzheimer's or dementia-related disorders for persons 60 or older), intellectual disabilities, brain injuries, and non-substance-abuse physical/mental/emotional disabilities.

headings.title: Training, alert policies, and agency response duties
headings.reviewNote: Directs DPS and partner agencies before July 1, 2027, to develop CIT training and a compatible alert system, establish missing-person response policies, and require media, officer, and surrounding-county notifications.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to administer and promulgate rules for the Purple Alert System subject to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2026 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 650.535 enacting RJ's Law, creating the Purple Alert System, defining developmental disability, setting a pre-July 1, 2027 training/policy mandate, and directing rulemaking (fixed wrong date 'July 1, 2024' and inaccurate text in sub. 4).

headings.title: Economic Distress Zone Fund creation and purpose
headings.reviewNote: Creates the dedicated Economic Distress Zone Fund for DPS funding of 501(c)(3) organizations providing crime-deterrence services in areas of high crime and deteriorating infrastructure.

headings.title: Three million dollar biennial reversion threshold
headings.reviewNote: Provides that appropriated moneys over three million dollars (excluding gifts, grants, bequests, or contributions) remaining at biennium end revert to general revenue notwithstanding section 33.080.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of public safety to promulgate implementing rules subject to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2021 nonseverability.

headings.title: Definition of high-crime deteriorating infrastructure areas
headings.reviewNote: Defines qualifying areas as cities with a homicide rate at least seven times the national FBI UCR average, poverty rate over 20%, and a school district with at least 80% free/reduced lunch eligibility.

headings.title: August 28, 2024 statutory termination date
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the provisions of this section shall terminate on August 28, 2024.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 650.550 creating the Economic Distress Zone Fund, $3M reversion threshold, rulemaking, statutory area definition, and August 28, 2024 termination date (rewrote all 5 fabricated draft headings).

headings.title: Task Force on Nonprofit Safety and Security
headings.reviewNote: Establishes Task Force on Nonprofit Safety and Security within the office of homeland security.

headings.title: Task force composition and nine-member appointments
headings.reviewNote: Directs the DPS director to appoint nine members: six ex officio directors/designees (homeland security, highway patrol, sheriffs, police chiefs, interfaith, nonprofits) and three nonprofit/faith/academic/counterterrorism representatives.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that task force members serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Election of task force chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Requires task force members to elect a chair by majority vote.

headings.title: Quarterly meetings and special sessions
headings.reviewNote: Directs task force to meet at least quarterly, with additional meetings upon call of the chair.

headings.title: Quorum and voting requirements for official action
headings.reviewNote: Establishes majority quorum requirement and mandates affirmative majority vote of members present for official action.

headings.title: Annual terrorism reports to legislative budget committees
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reports on terrorist threats to homeland security and legislative appropriations and budget committees.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 650.900 establishing the nine-member Missouri Task Force on Nonprofit Safety and Security, governance, meetings, quorum, and annual reporting (corrected wrong member count 'fifteen' -> 'nine' in sub. 2 and permissive reimbursement in sub. 3).

headings.title: Supplemental Nonprofit Safety and Security Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates dedicated fund in state treasury with nonreversion and investment earnings retention.

headings.title: Permitted expenditure uses for security enhancements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes grant funding for security planning, equipment, exercises, threat training, and structural upgrades.

headings.title: Eligibility tied to federal FEMA security grants
headings.reviewNote: Deems nonprofits approved under federal FEMA security grant program automatically eligible without separate application.

headings.title: Five percent maximum grant limitation per organization
headings.reviewNote: Caps individual organization grants at five percent of available funds and conditions awards on federal announcements.

headings.title: Five percent cap on annual administrative expenses
headings.reviewNote: Limits annual department administrative expenses to no more than five percent of available fund moneys.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to promulgate implementing rules subject to chapter 536 compliance and post-August 28, 2025 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 650.910 creating the Supplemental Nonprofit Safety and Security Fund, eligible security enhancements, FEMA grant eligibility, 5% grant and administrative caps, and rulemaking.
